keyframe_review.note: 41,725 km2 (resolves to 173 cells, 43.8 thousand km2): Fife, Perthshire, Angus, Aberdeenshire, Moray, the Highlands to the Dornoch Firth and Argyll. The page gives no area. It describes Alba as 'extending only between the Firth of Forth and the River Spey' and says 'Moray was not considered part of Alba until the early 13th century', while 'Fortriu was added in the tenth century'; the shape holds all 12 Moray cells and 67 of 108 Highland cells from 900. Flagged in notes, not corrected: the page gives no year for Moray.

42,040 km2: the 900 shape with one cell changed (253 km2, at the Northumbrian edge). unverified: page budget. Alba page: Indulf (954-962) captured oppidum Eden, 'almost certainly Edinburgh', 'the first Scottish foothold in Lothian'.

49,027 km2: +31 cells (7.8 thousand km2) of the Borders, Lothian and the Tweed valley (Scottish Borders 20, East Lothian 3, Midlothian 2, Edinburgh 1). Bernicia page: '973 ... Scots sovereignty over northern Bernicia, now known as Lothian, was acknowledged by Edgar of England'; the Carham page records historians dating the transfer to Edgar's 'beneficence' in the 970s or to Carham in 1018 ('probably incomplete until at least the 1070s').

58,537 km2: the 1034 shape, 42 km2 larger by raster. unverified: page budget; Abernethy (1072) is on no page opened.

59,455 km2: +3 cells (two in Argyll that Cliopatria draws in the Isles, one other) and one cell lost in the Highlands. unverified: page budget; no opened page dates a change on the western coast at this date. The English counties David I took are not in this shape: see the new keyframes 1136 and 1139.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1136-1138: the 1099 shape with Carlisle and Cumberland. David I page: 'by the end of January [1136], he had occupied the castles of Carlisle, Wark, Alnwick, Norham and Newcastle'; the First Durham treaty (February 1136): 'David would retain Carlisle'; the Battle of the Standard (22 August 1138) was 'a defeat for the Scots'. Cliopatria's Alba row never draws England.

correction.text: Alba with Cumberland and the earldom of Northumberland (Henry's), 1139-1156

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1139-1156: the 1099 shape with Cumberland and the earldom of Northumberland. David I page (Second Treaty of Durham): 'David's son Henry was given the earldom of Northumberland' and 'David himself was allowed to keep Carlisle and Cumberland'; Bamburgh and Newcastle stayed with Stephen; during the Anarchy David held 'dominion over all of England north-west of the river Ribble and Pennines' and the north-east 'as far south as the river Tyne' (undated). Malcolm IV was made to give them up in 1157 (Malcolm IV page).

64,924 km2: +19 cells (4.8 thousand km2) that are Cliopatria's Galloway land (Dumfries and Galloway 13, South Ayrshire 4, East Ayrshire 1). Lordship of Galloway page: 'upon his death in 1234, his holdings were divided between his three daughters and their husbands' (Anglo-Normans); 'Galloway's period as an independent political entity eventually came to an end with John de Balliol delegated as Lord'. The Treaty of York (25 September 1237) 'established the Anglo-Scottish border in a form that remains almost unchanged to modern times'.

85,304 km2 (resolves to 321 cells, 81.2 thousand km2): +57 cells (14.4 thousand km2): the Hebrides (Eilean Siar 9), Argyll's islands and the Highland coast (Highland 37, Argyll and Bute 9). Treaty of Perth page: 'signed 2 July 1266', settling 'possession of the Hebrides and the Isle of Man'; 'Scotland confirmed Norwegian sovereignty over Shetland and Orkney'. The shape does not hold the Isle of Man; the page does not say what happened there. Six years after the treaty.
85,304 km2, the 1272 shape. The page ends Alba with Alexander III in 1286; Cliopatria keeps the row to 1293 and starts the Kingdom of Scotland in 1294 (separate dossier).

region.text: Alba, the Pictish kingdom with Dalriada, 'between the Firth of Forth and the River Spey' and beyond

ledger.note: 900: the kingdom of Alba. 'Donald II ... the first man to have been called ri Alban', died 900 at Dunnottar; the page dates the kingdom 'between the deaths of Donald II in 900 and of Alexander III in 1286'. Constantine II follows (900-943 on other pages). The region is Cliopatria's shape; the page gives the Forth-Spey core.

region.text: Lothian and the Borders: Edinburgh, the Lothians and Scottish Borders cells that Cliopatria adds in 980

ledger.note: 973: Edgar acknowledges Scottish sovereignty over Lothian. 'Scots sovereignty over northern Bernicia, now known as Lothian, was acknowledged by Edgar of England' (Bernicia page); the Carham page says historians date the transfer either to Edgar's 'beneficence' in the 970s or to the Scottish victory at Carham (1018) and that the takeover was 'probably incomplete until at least the 1070s'. The England dossier has the matching loss at 973. Cliopatria draws the land from 980.

region.text: the Strathclyde shape: Clydesdale, Ayrshire and eastern Galloway, exactly Cliopatria's Strathclyde row

ledger.note: 1034: the Scots take Strathclyde. 'Conquered by the Scots, most probably during the reign of Maol Coluim mac Cinaeda who died in 1034'; Cliopatria's Strathclyde row ends 1033 and its Alba shape of 1034 adds exactly the Strathclyde cells.

region.text: three cells on the western coast, two in Argyll

ledger.note: 1099: Cliopatria adds three cells on the western coast (two in Argyll that it draws in the Isles) and drops one in the Highlands. The Alba page records no change on the western coast at this date: page silent.

region.text: the earldom of Northumberland, without Bamburgh and Newcastle

ledger.note: January 1136: David I invades England. 'By the end of January, he had occupied the castles of Carlisle, Wark, Alnwick, Norham and Newcastle' after Henry I's death (1135); the page records no fighting.

region.text: the earldom of Northumberland, without Bamburgh and Newcastle

ledger.note: February 1136: the First Treaty of Durham. 'A treaty was agreed whereby David would retain Carlisle', with Henry's title and half the Huntingdon lands restored to his son; the page implies the northern castles (Wark, Alnwick, Norham, Newcastle) went back to Stephen.

February 1136: David keeps Carlisle. 'A treaty was agreed whereby David would retain Carlisle'; the page names Carlisle only; the whole of Cumbria is the researcher's reading of Carlisle and Cumberland. The Norman England dossier has the matching loss at 1136 and 1139.

region.text: the earldom of Northumberland, without Bamburgh and Newcastle

ledger.note: 1139: the Second Treaty of Durham gives the earldom of Northumberland to David's son Henry. 'David's son Henry was given the earldom of Northumberland' and 'David himself was allowed to keep Carlisle and Cumberland'; 'the strategically vital castles of Bamburgh and Newcastle' stayed with Stephen. The page gives the date by sequence, not by year.

union.text: the earldom of Northumberland, without Bamburgh and Newcastle

region.text: Cumbria and Northumbria, held by David I from 1136 and 1139

ledger.note: 1157: Henry II takes back the north. Malcolm IV did homage 'in 1157 at Peveril Castle in Derbyshire and later at Chester'; 'Henry II refused to allow Malcolm to keep Cumbria, or William to keep Northumbria', granting Malcolm the Earldom of Huntingdon instead. The page does not describe a surrender of Carlisle, Newcastle or Bamburgh in 1157, and does not mention Westmorland.

region.text: Galloway: Dumfries and Galloway and Ayrshire cells that Cliopatria adds in 1236

ledger.note: 1234: Galloway comes under the Scottish crown. 'Upon his death in 1234, his holdings were divided between his three daughters and their husbands' (Anglo-Normans); 'Galloway's period as an independent political entity eventually came to an end with John de Balliol delegated as Lord'. The page gives no year for the revolt of Gille Ruadh or for Alexander II's action. Cliopatria draws Galloway in Alba from 1236.

ledger.note: 1263: the war with Norway for the Hebrides opens at Largs. 'The treaty was agreed three years after the Battle of Largs in 1263'; Hakon IV's forces at Largs, 'the result was inconclusive'.

region.text: the Hebrides, Skye and the western seaboard that Cliopatria adds in 1272

ledger.note: 2 July 1266: the Treaty of Perth ends the war. 'The Treaty of Perth, signed 2 July 1266, ended military conflict' between Magnus the Lawmender of Norway and Alexander III.

region.text: the Hebrides, Skye and the western seaboard that Cliopatria adds in 1272

ledger.note: 2 July 1266: the Hebrides pass to Scotland. The treaty settled 'possession of the Hebrides and the Isle of Man'; 'Scotland confirmed Norwegian sovereignty over Shetland and Orkney'; the page gives 4,000 marks and an annuity of 100 marks for the settlement. Cliopatria draws the land in Alba from 1272; the page does not say what happened to the Isle of Man.

1286: Alexander III dies and the Alba period ends. The page dates the kingdom 'between the deaths of Donald II in 900 and of Alexander III in 1286' and calls the name Alba 'one of convenience'; it does not date a change of name to Scotland. Same state and colour: Cliopatria continues the row to 1293 and then names it Kingdom of Scotland.

1293: the Alba row ends in Cliopatria and the Kingdom of Scotland row begins in 1294. The Alba page names no event in 1293 or 1294 (it mentions Edward I's invasion of 1296, 'linked indirectly to Alexander III's death'); the year is Cliopatria's.

wars.outcome: Malcolm IV gives up Cumbria and Northumbria to Henry II in 1157; William the Lion is captured at Alnwick in 1174 (Alba page); on 25 September 1237 the Treaty of York has Alexander II 'quitclaim to the King of England his hereditary rights to the counties of Northumberland, Cumberland, and Westmorland' and 'established the Anglo-Scottish border in a form that remains almost unchanged'.

wars.outcome: Inconclusive Battle of Largs (1263); the Treaty of Perth (2 July 1266) gives the Hebrides and the Isle of Man to Scotland and leaves Orkney and Shetland to Norway for 4,000 marks and an annuity of 100 marks.

certainty.note: No frontier is dated by treaty or survey on the pages opened. The English frontier moved with David I's conquests (1136-1157) and is not drawn in Cliopatria's shapes; the Spey and Moray limits are described, not dated.

The Treaty of York (25 September 1237) 'officially defined' the Anglo-Scottish border 'for the first time and by mutual agreement'; the Treaty of Perth (2 July 1266) fixes the Norwegian frontier at Orkney and Shetland. The Highland, Moray and Galloway internal limits stay soft.

notes: Ten pages cited, six of them opened for this state (budget five) because the state spans 394 years and nine shapes; four are shared with the Bernicia, Strathclyde and Northumbria dossiers. Not settled: (1) Moray. The Alba page says Alba extended 'only between the Firth of Forth and the River Spey' and that 'Moray was not considered part of Alba until the early 13th century', but Cliopatria's 900 shape holds all of Moray and 67 of 108 Highland cells (to 57.97 N); the same page says 'Fortriu was added in the tenth century'. No year is given, so the shape was not cut. A gap-filler should tint Moray as a vassal or cut it until the 13th century. (2) The English counties. Cliopatria never draws David I's Cumbria and Northumberland (1136-1157); the new keyframes 1136 and 1139 add them. The Norman England dossier may still draw them in its own shape: reconcile. The page for 1092 (William Rufus at Carlisle) was not opened, so the Norman England loss/gain pair 1092 has no Alba side. (3) The Isle of Man: the Treaty of Perth settles it but Cliopatria's Alba shape never holds it and the Kingdom of Mann row ends 1271. (4) Not opened (page budget): Abernethy 1072, Cnut and Malcolm II about 1031 (the North Sea Empire dossier has the vassal tie), Treaty of Falaise 1174 and Canterbury 1189 (the Angevin dossier has them), the 1098 treaty with Magnus Barelegs. The Alba page says the Scottish kings 'were not independent monarchs, but vassals to the King of the English', in a sentence with no date. (5) The page puts the end of Alba at Alexander III's death (1286); Cliopatria's row runs to 1293. Capitals and rulers are omitted: the page fetch showed no infobox and no capital, and no list page was opened (the inauguration place Scone appears on the David I and Malcolm IV pages but is not called a capital). Disagreements: Carham 1018 or 1016; Lothian by Edgar (970s) or Carham (1018); Galloway 1234 (Lordship page) vs Cliopatria 1236 vs 1135 revolt on the Alba page. Quotation marks enclose strings the page-fetch tool returned as quotations; other wording paraphrases its summary of the page, which was read by WebFetch only (no raw page text).
